judgement.why: The requirement demands obtaining and enforcing depth as canonical_bytes defines it, but the imported contract exposes only canonicalisation to bytes and no depth result or limit parameter.

topics.topic: What response id to use when rejecting an excessively deep request body
questions: For an over-depth JSON object containing a string or integer id, must the implementation parse or walk enough of the body to return that id, or must the depth-refusal response use null without applying the every-response id rule?

quotes: After the token check, before any other bound is checked and before the message is parsed, walked or canonicalised, the depth of the request message as received, as canonical_bytes defines depth, MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, measured on the message text without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
judgement.why: An over-depth body must be rejected before the message is parsed or walked, while the every-response rule requires determining whether that body is an object and reading its id.
